key_insight: In a Houston 2024 simulation replay, a county-risk reserve rule raised observed five-hour battery backup coverage from 75.0% to 86.5% and added $10.2 in modeled annualized margin per home versus a fixed 20% reserve.
engineering_relevance: Risk-adaptive battery reserves can help residential fleet operators evaluate electricity-market revenue and household backup service together.
method: Release HomeFleet-ERCOT, combining observed prices and county outages with explicitly simulated homes and causal controller inputs.
Compare independent-home optimization with 21 PPO training runs and 10 promise-cost candidates.
Evaluate transfer across time, geography, fleets, and storms, plus synthetic warning and battery stress tests.
evidence_signal: The paired 95% margin interval was +$1.7 to +$21.7 per home, while the paired coverage-gain interval included zero; all 10 promise-cost candidates had lower modeled margin than the fixed-reserve baseline.
watch_item: Results are conditional simulations, not measured company reliability; only 19.5% of 41 county mass-outage episodes offered enough continuous warning for every battery preset.
paper_title: Adaptive Reliability Reserves for Residential Battery Fleets
